gen-gf-phudu-fs-ranade: Bold, with a ballpoint's pressure-free line and curves that open generously at the ends. Ranade follows in a plain sans whose stems run slightly heavier than its crossbars, with a gentle rubber-cord wobble in the weight.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-supreme: Phudu draws everything as if with one nib, low and wide, its curves left open at the ends. And Supreme stands taller and denser beneath it, crisp and sturdy, so the two feel like a sketch next to a stamp.
gen-gf-phudu-general-sans:
Distinctive from the first glance, Phudu is low and loose-ended.

General Sans sits under it with a tall x-height that fills each line, and its smooth bends give the heading's bent-tubing shapes a roomy, steady partner.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-orbit: Orbit keeps its curves from closing and floats each character apart from its neighbors. Orbit's rope-like stems hold up as sans-serif body text, while a Phudu heading made small would lose the bend and bounce that make it bold.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-syncopate: Bold and rounded, Phudu is built to announce, its curves left generously open at the ends. But Syncopate does the quieter job, laying out open, technical-pen letters with rung-like spacing that keeps the text moving.
gen-gf-phudu-manrope: Chunky, open-mouthed and friendly, Phudu looks like it was drawn with a ballpoint that never pressed hard. Manrope's bright curve gaps keep a long page of sans-serif text easy going.
gen-gf-phudu-montserrat: Phudu's curves all end in generous openings, like a ballpoint line lifted early. Montserrat adds oversized, white-filled counters beneath, and the gliding wire-like line makes a bright, sturdy partner for that bold heading.
gen-gf-phudu-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall and friendly, with a soaring x-height and a wide e that never pinches shut. And Phudu, low and bold above it, gives that sans-serif text a distinctive, ballpoint-drawn headline to lean on.
gen-gf-phudu-switzer: Phudu's ballpoint-plain line opens every curve generously, giving it a bold, bendy look. Switzer's tall waist line and tubular wire-like letters make a sans that moves steadily along, with each c tip kept well apart.
gen-gf-phudu-work-sans:
Bold and distinctive, Phudu draws every curve open with a plain ballpoint line.

Work Sans sits high on its mean line with sturdy joins, so a plain sans body would crowd Phudu if the heading were made small.
